newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco copper production falls in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Codelco copper production falls in first quarter.

text.p: Copper production at state company Codelco slipped to 291,697 tonnes metal content in the first quarter of the year from 296,031 tonnes in the first quarter of last year, the company said.
It attributed the fall to lower mineral grades. Two of its four mines reported production declines, while Chuquicamata and Salvador reported modestly higher output rates in the first quarter.

"Production has declined slightly mainly because of mining in areas of lower mineral grades, which was partly countered by greater mineral treatment rates (at processing plants)," said Codelco in a statement.

The company, which is entirely owned by the state, reported profits of $350 million in the first quarter of the year, down from $433 million in the first quarter of 1996. Last year's figure, however, included a once-off sum of $137 million from the sale of part of the company's Tocopilla electrical plant to a Belgian-Spanish-Chilean consortium.
